facts.fact: Africa50 and Bayobab (MTN Group) partnered in May 2023 to co-develop Project East2West, a US$320-325 million terrestrial fibre network linking landlocked countries to coastal cables, with the Republic of Congo among the 12 countries named (Kenya, South Sudan, CAR, Congo, Tanzania, Rwanda, Uganda, DRC, Mozambique, Malawi, Zambia, Angola); Africa50's investment committee approved it on 21 July 2023.

systems.platform: terrestrial fibre optic network (dark and active fibre)
systems.owner: Bayobab (MTN GlobalConnect Solutions), majority sponsor; Africa50 co-developer; Smart Africa Alliance technical partner

facts.fact: Xalam Analytics' January 2026 brief describes the Central African Backbone project as ongoing to expand Congo's fibre backbone, connecting to secondary towns and neighbouring countries; the brief gives no date for the work beyond its own January 2026 publication, taken as the date.

Xalam Analytics' January 2026 brief states that submarine cables have been deployed across the Congo river to connect Brazzaville and Kinshasa (DRC); no date for the deployment is given, so the brief's January 2026 publication date is used.

systems.country_label: Submarine cables across the Congo river

facts.fact: On 6 February 2023 the Central African Republic inaugurated its national fibre backbone and its interconnection with the Republic of Congo (via Bomassa), part of the 935 km of installed and operational fibre under the AfDB and EU supported Central African Backbone project, with a Congolese telecoms ministry representative present; the release says this component completes the Cameroon and Congo components.

The Treasury sheet says Congo has been connected to Cameroon through the CAB project since 2022.
The Treasury sheet says Congo Telecom's underwater river cable has linked Brazzaville to Kinshasa in the DRC since 2017.
